analysts.summary: The consensus average ($618.51) and median ($616) sit at or just below the current price. Targets are being chased higher: BofA's Vivek Arya went to $720 from $620 on Sep 25, Bernstein is at $650 (Sep 22), Raymond James at $641, Piper Sandler at $600 and Truist at $594. Consensus EPS: 2026E $7.58, 2027E $15.58.

bear: Valuation: ~161x TTM, ~83x 2026E and ~40x 2027E, vs NVDA at ~19x forward. The stock is at the consensus target after a ~195% YTD run.
Execution risk: any MI450 slip, power-efficiency gap or utilization shortfall on gigawatt deals would hit a price that assumes perfection.
Customer concentration and the hyperscaler capex cycle. China export curbs weigh on accelerator sales.
Gaming down 31% y/y. Higher PC prices are hurting desktop demand.
Persistent CEO 10b5-1 selling. A drop below the ~$593 zero-gamma level could accelerate a pullback.
bull: Data center revenue doubled (+107% y/y). The Helios/MI450 ramp starts now, backed by multi-gigawatt commitments from OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic and Oracle.
Consensus expects 2027 EPS to double to ~$15.58. At ~40x, a beat-and-raise path could re-rate toward the $720-780 bull targets.
~10% price increases in Q4 and a mix shift to data center support 56%+ gross margins.
Record server CPU share, and agentic AI (e.g., Meta's Muse) is lifting CPU demand alongside GPUs.
Net cash balance sheet and ~$8.4B TTM FCF.

catalysts.event: Helios / MI450 (MI455X) rack shipments begin at end of Q3 and ramp through Q4 into 1H27
catalysts.why: First revenue from the OpenAI (6 GW), Meta (up to 6 GW), Anthropic (up to 2 GW) and Oracle (50k GPU) commitments. This is the core of the bull case.

catalysts.event: ~10% price increases on AI accelerators, GPUs and chipsets (TrendForce, Sep 18)
catalysts.why: Passes through TSMC's ~10% foundry cost increase and should support gross margin near or above 56%.
Extends server CPU share gains as agentic AI adds CPU demand.
Guide is ~$13B. The Q4 guide and MI450 ramp commentary will decide whether the ~40x 2027 multiple holds.
Keeps the annual roadmap cadence against NVIDIA.

competition.summary: AMD is the clear #2 in merchant AI accelerators behind NVIDIA and is taking x86 share from Intel. Its edge is supplying both the CPU (EPYC) and the GPU (Instinct) in a full Helios rack with open ROCm software. Broadcom and hyperscaler custom ASICs compete for the same AI capex dollars.

insiders.summary: Insider activity is selling only. CEO Lisa Su keeps selling under a 10b5-1 plan adopted June 8 2026. She still holds ~3.0M shares directly plus ~0.85M indirectly. We found no insider purchases.

institutions.summary: Institutions own ~74% of AMD. The largest holders are the passive giants (BlackRock 150.3M shares, Vanguard 106.5M, State Street 74.4M). Q2 2026 13Fs were split: Citadel (+155%), Renaissance (+282%) and a new Tiger Global stake on the buy side; Bridgewater (-58%), Millennium (-40%) and Appaloosa (-11%) trimmed. 13F data lags by 1.5-4.5 months and predates the September rally.

options.gexNote: Net dealer gamma is positive (~+$18M per 1% move) across the $580-680 strikes of the two nearest expiries, sampled at $10 steps. The largest positive GEX is at $650 (call wall). Heavy put OI at $600 (4,106 contracts) makes the largest negative node there (put wall). Gamma flips negative near ~$593, so a drop below $600 could speed up. Above that level, dealer hedging should dampen moves between $600 and $650.
options.ivNote: Underlying IV is 50.4% vs 30-day realized vol of 49.3%. The IV percentile is low (17th over 13 weeks, 17th over 52 weeks), so options are cheap relative to their own history despite the rally. Option volume is running below average: 289k calls / 240k puts today vs 418k / 312k average.
options.strategy: Educational idea, not an order. With IV cheap and the price above fair-value midpoint, a defined-risk structure fits better than chasing stock. For example, a Nov call spread above the $650 call wall to participate in a post-earnings MI450 beat, or selling $590-600 puts only if you'd be happy to own AMD near the put wall and zero-gamma zone. Earnings (~Nov 3) sit inside the Nov expiry.

summary: AMD is executing well. Q2 2026 revenue rose 50% to $11.5B, data center revenue doubled, and Q3 is guided to about $13B as Helios/MI450 racks start shipping. After a roughly 195% YTD run to about $631 (a $1T market cap), the stock trades at about 40x 2027 consensus EPS of $15.58 and sits right around the analyst average target of about $619. Our blended fair value of $520-670 (midpoint $600) puts the price inside the range. We read it as fairly valued: the business case is strong, but the price already assumes a flawless MI450 ramp. We'd stay Neutral and add on pullbacks toward the $590-600 gamma/put-wall zone rather than chase the move.

valuation.method: Three methods blended. (a) Peer multiples: AMD's EPS is expected to double in 2027, so it earns a growth premium over NVDA and AVGO (~19-20x forward). Applying 32-42x to 2027E EPS of $15.58 gives $499-654. (b) Earnings power: 2028 revenue of ~$122B (2027E $88B +38%), 35-40% non-GAAP operating margin, 13% tax and 1.65B shares gives $22-26 EPS. At 28-32x, discounted 2 years at 10%, that is ~$519-677. (c) Analysts: 55 analysts, average target ~$619, median $616, range $365-1,250. Blended fair value: $520-670, midpoint $600.
valuation.note: Multiples are from stockanalysis.com statistics pages read on Sep 26 2026. AMD's forward P/E of 57 is on next-twelve-months estimates; on 2027 consensus it is ~40x. Intel's TTM P/E is n/a because TTM net income was negative.
